source.title: Stable and low-precision training for large-scale vision-language models
source.authors: Mitchell Wortsman; Tim Dettmers; Luke Zettlemoyer; Ari S. Morcos; Ali Farhadi; Ludwig Schmidt

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, including appendices; no obvious cutoff or garbling that prevents reading the relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports training outcomes for CLIP models under quantization and optimizer-stability interventions. Those experiments do not measure training classification error, bad local minima, depth/shortcut effects, initialization-dependent trainability, edge-of-stability recovery, or batch-normalization speed as defined in V1–V6.
record.gate_note: Its reported accuracy is zero-shot ImageNet accuracy and its stability measure is loss spikes/loss curves, not training classification error. It does not test the listed claim versions. Results that only compare SwitchBack speed or accuracy against low-precision baselines are outside the versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures low-precision CLIP training, optimizer-related loss spikes, and zero-shot ImageNet accuracy. It does not test V1–V6. Zero-initialized layer-scale is evaluated in residual transformers under quantization, without a plain-network initialization, training-speed, or trainable-depth comparison for V4. Loss-spike experiments do not measure curvature or establish learning rates relative to a stability threshold for V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: SwitchBack accelerates low-precision CLIP training, and StableAdamW avoids loss spikes at the tested scales while outperforming gradient clipping in zero-shot accuracy. The authors acknowledge non-exhaustive experiments, simulated float8 arithmetic, and low checkpoint accuracy from limited compute.
record.recipe_differences: The study tests low-precision linear layers and optimizer interventions in CLIP training, rather than the training-error, initialization, depth, stability-limit, or batch-normalization recipes in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Loss spikes vary with model size, batch size, learning rate, and AdamW β2; RMS-to-loss-spike prediction is shown for the patch embedding layer but not a middle transformer layer. These findings concern loss instability rather than any listed version's outcome.

fits_no_version.finding: In simulated tensor-wise fp8 CLIP ViT-Large training, zero-initialized layer-scale prevents divergence, whereas the baseline, gradient clipping, and KQ layer normalization do not. Layer-scale also controls feature magnitudes in later blocks (Section 2.3, Figure 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Controlling feature magnitudes with zero-initialized residual scaling can enable tensor-wise fp8 training of CLIP transformers.

fits_no_version.finding: CLIP loss spikes increase with model size, batch size, and learning rate. Lowering AdamW β2 mitigates spikes but can slow learning; patch-embedding second-moment estimation failures predict spikes. StableAdamW removes instability at the tested scales and exceeds gradient clipping in zero-shot accuracy (Sections 3.3–3.5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stale AdamW second-moment estimates can precede CLIP loss spikes, and update clipping can stabilize training.

fits_no_version.finding: SwitchBack int8 training provides 13–25% end-to-end speedups for CLIP ViT-Huge while remaining within 0.1 percentage points of bfloat16 zero-shot ImageNet accuracy (Section 2.2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selective higher-precision weight-gradient computation enables faster int8 CLIP training with little zero-shot accuracy loss.

record.code_released: https://github.com/TimDettmers/bitsandbytes/ (Triton kernels; the text also links to OpenCLIP and benchmark code)
record.problems: The authors state the work is non-exhaustive, float8 is simulated rather than run on float8 hardware, and produced checkpoints have low accuracy due to limited compute. The central results for the listed claim versions are not measured.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: the study does not report a result measuring any listed version's outcome.

untested.parts: Training classification error in convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels and model-size or training-recipe effects.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks and their dependence on extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation in plain networks and its prevention by identity shortcuts; very deep plain tanh and Fixup training.
Activation-matched initialization effects on plain-network learning speed and trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Recovery or divergence relative to an initial stability threshold, curvature reduction, and full-batch edge-of-stability dynamics.
Batch normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance; comparable training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's relation from tests to discusses; retain T6. The empty result-row set is appropriate for V1–V6. Related findings above do not justify verdicts on those versions.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR benchmarks, corrupted or random labels, model size, and training duration.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the effect of student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual network training error across depth on ImageNet or CIFAR-10; Fixup without normalization is mentioned only as related work.
Activation-matched initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, signal/gradient propagation, and trainable depth.
Training above a linearized stability limit and sharpness behavior at the edge of stability.
Batch normalization's effect on training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup's performance relative to normalization.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
